# How to use Nano Banana 2.1 in Picsart for AI image generation

> **In short:** Nano Banana 2.1 is Google's latest image model, now inside Picsart's AI Playground. You can generate images from text, edit photos, and refine them in one chat — but you'll need a paid Picsart plan, and the tool only works on still images.

If you've ever opened Picsart to make a quick poster, clean up a photo, or design a thumbnail, the engine under the hood just got an upgrade. Google's new Nano Banana 2.1 model now sits inside Picsart's AI Playground — the part of the app where you create and edit images with AI. It can read your text, look at your photos, and let you keep tweaking the result in the same conversation. Here's how to start, even if you've never used an AI image tool before.

## Before you start
- A Picsart account — sign-up is free, but **AI image generation usually sits behind a paid plan**. Check Picsart's current pricing page before you begin.
- The Picsart app on phone or tablet, or the web version in your browser.
- A rough idea of what you want to make: a poster, a product mock-up, a quick photo edit.
- About 10 minutes for your first image.

## Step 1 — Open Picsart and find the AI Playground
Open the Picsart app and sign in. On the home screen, look for an entry called **AI Playground**, **AI Image Generator**, or something similar — that's the part of the app dedicated to AI-powered image creation. If you can't spot it on the home grid, tap the **+** button or look for a **Create** tab, then browse the AI tools there. On the web version, you'll usually find it under a top-menu item like **AI Tools** or **Create**.

💬 Example: this step has nothing to type — just finding the right place to start.

You'll know it worked when you see a prompt box (a text field where you describe the image you want) and an option to either start from text or upload your own picture.

## Step 2 — Select Nano Banana 2.1 as your model
Once you're inside the AI Playground, look for a **model selector** — it might be a dropdown at the top, a small chip near the prompt box, or a tile inside a side menu. Picsart usually offers several AI models side by side; choose **Nano Banana 2.1** (sometimes labeled **Nano Banana v2.1**). If you don't see it in the list, the model may not yet be available on your device, account type, or region — check Picsart's release notes or support page for the latest.

💬 Example: not a typing step, but the key choice is **Nano Banana 2.1**, not any other model in the list.

You'll know it worked when "Nano Banana 2.1" appears as the active model name near the prompt box.

## Step 3 — Pick your canvas (aspect ratio and resolution)
Before you write your prompt, choose the **shape and size** of the image. Look for an **aspect ratio** setting (Picsart offers up to 15 options — like 1:1 for Instagram, 9:16 for stories, 16:9 for a banner) and a **resolution** setting (1K, 2K or 4K — higher means sharper but takes longer and uses more of your plan's allowance). For a quick social-media post, 1K at 1:1 is plenty. For a poster you might print, 2K or 4K is safer.

💬 Example: for a square Instagram post, choose **1:1** and **1K**; for a phone wallpaper, choose **9:16** and **2K**.

You'll know it worked when the canvas preview — or the chosen numbers — shows the dimensions you picked.

## Step 4 — Write your prompt and generate
In the prompt box, describe the picture you want in plain language. Be specific about the subject, the mood, the colours, and anything you want readable as text on the image — Nano Banana 2.1 handles text on posters and diagrams well, which is one of its advertised strengths. Then tap the **Generate** button (it may also be called **Create**, or shown as an arrow icon). After a few seconds, one or more image options appear. Pick the one you like best, or regenerate if none feel right.

💬 Example: "A friendly poster for a Saturday morning yoga class, pastel colours, with the words 'Saturday Morning Yoga' clearly readable in the centre."

You'll know it worked when a finished image appears on screen and matches the dimensions you chose in Step 3.

## Step 5 — Refine the image in the same chat
This is where Nano Banana 2.1 stands out: you don't have to start over when something's off. Stay in the **same conversation** and send a follow-up message describing the change. The model keeps the rest of the picture intact and adjusts only what you asked for. You can chain several refinements one after another — change colours, swap a background, add a logo, rewrite the text — without losing the previous version.

💬 Example: after the yoga poster above, send: "Make the background soft pink, change the words to 'Bring a friend!', and add a small sun in the top corner."

You'll know it worked when the new image shows your specific change and the rest of the picture still looks like the previous one.

## Step 6 — Edit an existing photo (optional)
If you want to change a picture you already have instead of generating a new one, look for an **Upload** or **Image** button near the prompt box (sometimes shown as a picture icon or a + sign). Pick the photo from your device, then describe the edit you want in the prompt box. Nano Banana 2.1 can also be guided by a quick doodle — paint over the part you want changed and write a short note next to it. Be precise: say exactly what to remove, replace, or add. The model can also combine several uploaded images into a single new scene.

💬 Example: upload a group photo, then write: "Remove the person in the red shirt on the right." Or paint over the background and write: "Replace this background with a sunset beach."

You'll know it worked when the edited photo appears with your change applied and the rest of the image still looks natural.

## Step 7 — Save and export
When you're happy with the result, look for a **Save**, **Download**, or **Export** button — usually at the top-right of the image or inside a **⋯** menu. Picsart may ask you to pick a file format: choose **JPG** for everyday sharing, or **PNG** if you need a transparent background. The image then saves to your device's gallery or your computer's Downloads folder. If you want to keep editing later in Picsart, look for a **Save to project** option instead.

💬 Example: not a typing step, but the key choice is **JPG** for everyday sharing, **PNG** only if you need a transparent background.

You'll know it worked when the image file appears in your phone's gallery (or your computer's Downloads folder) and opens like any normal picture.

## Common mistakes
- **Picking the wrong model.** Picsart shows several AI engines side by side. If your image looks dull or the text comes out garbled, double-check that **Nano Banana 2.1** is the selected model — not an older one — and regenerate.
- **Asking for vague edits in Step 5.** "Make it better" gives the model nothing to act on. Always name the specific change: a colour, an object, a word, a mood. The more concrete the instruction, the closer the result.
- **Forgetting the cost.** Each generation usually spends credits or counts against your plan's allowance. A 4K image costs more than a 1K one, and multi-turn refinement counts as extra generations. Check your remaining credits before kicking off a long chain of edits — otherwise the model may stop mid-conversation.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** You can make a custom birthday card, a flyer for a school bake sale, or a fun wallpaper for your phone — in minutes, without any design training.
- **For your business or work:** You can mock up a quick social-media post, an event poster, or a product visual to share with a colleague before commissioning a designer for the final version.
- **If you're just getting started:** Begin with one simple text-to-image prompt (Step 4) at 1K resolution. Get a feel for what the model does well before moving on to edits or 4K output.

## Try it now
Open Picsart, find the AI Playground, and generate one square (1:1) 1K image of your favourite season — a single sentence prompt, no edits, just see what comes back. Takes about two minutes.
